summary: On-prem proxy header folding trims Authorization token, causing intermittent 401/403 in private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customer AsterHealth reports intermittent 401/403 when calling Redwood Private inference endpoints. Errors correlate with requests that traverse their on-prem HTTP proxy. Impact: Several production endpoints for routing inference requests are failing ~3-7% of traffic causing degraded user experience for API consumers. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed ingress), prod-us-east. Observed behavior: Token exchange attempts fail with 401 from identity-proxy; Redwood logs show Authorization header value truncated at first space. Expected behavior: Full Bearer token should be forwarded intact and validated by identity service.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer issues curl request through on-prem proxy: curl -x http://proxy:8080 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <LONG_TOKEN>' https://private-api.customer.redwood/v1/generate
2) Some requests return 401 with response body {"error":"invalid_token"}, other requests succeed (intermittent).
3) Direct curl to private endpoint (bypassing proxy) succeeds every time.
4) Packet capture at proxy shows header value split across two lines (folded) where a CRLF SP insertion occurs within token string.
logs: ingress-proxy (2026-03-13T15:02:11Z) - forwarded header: 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9\r\n  abcdef...'
identity-proxy (2026-03-13T15:02:11Z) - token parse failed: token contains unexpected whitespace -> returning 401
application logs show 401 and 403 spikes that align with proxy flow start times (see dashboard: /dashboards/ingress/401-spike-AsterHealth)
investigation_notes: Checked Redwood ingress and identity-proxy traces; token is valid when received directly from customer app but appears truncated/contains whitespace when forwarded via on-prem proxy.

Packet capture from customer's proxy shows header folding (HTTP line folding) - a historical behavior where proxies insert CRLF+SP for long headers. This is deprecated in HTTP/1.1 and leads to the token containing a literal newline+space sequence which our token parser rejects.

Customer confirmed proxy is an older F5 BIG-IP configuration with 'allow-http-folding' behavior enabled in the intermediary iRules. Proxy vendor docs indicate toggles exist to disable header folding or to normalize headers.

Reproduced locally by configuring an nginx reverse proxy with 'proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization; more_clear_input_headers...' and forcing injection of CRLF SP - token parsing fails similarly.
Temporal correlation: incidents started after customer upgraded proxy firmware to a build that changed default header handling (03/10/2026).
comments: Priya Shah (Support) 2026-03-13: Raised initial ticket after customer report. Collected traces and asked for pcap. Requested exact proxy model and firmware.
AsterHealth SRE (customer) 2026-03-13: Attached pcap and proxy config snippet. Confirmed recent firmware change on appliance. Asked if Redwood can tolerate folded headers.
Maya Chen (Eng) 2026-03-13: Ran local repro, confirmed token parser rejects whitespace. Opening internal issue to add clearer logging for folded headers. Assigned INT-448 for infra follow-up.
AsterHealth SRE 2026-03-14: Applied temporary workaround on proxy (disabled header folding) and reported immediate reduction to 0.2% failure rate.
root_cause: On-prem proxy inserts HTTP header line folding (CRLF SP) into Authorization header for long values. Identity/token parser treats whitespace as invalid and returns 401. The customer's proxy firmware default changed behavior in a recent upgrade.
resolution: Workaround provided: Customer updated F5 iRule and disabled header folding behavior and validated end-to-end. Short-term: advised customer to upgrade proxy to vendor patch that preserves header single-line semantics or apply config flag to disable folding. Long-term: internal change: ingress now detects folded header sequences and emits a 400 with explicit 'folded-authorization' code and guidance to customer instead of returning generic 401; created PR github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/pull/612 to add debug logging and a clearer error message. Runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SITE/Proxy+compatibility+runbook. Follow-up task INT-448 created to consider tolerant header normalization with strict validation for downstream auth (pending security review).
resolution_notes: Customer applied workaround at 2026-03-14 09:18 UTC; support observed immediate reduction in errors.
Added temporary alert on ingress for any Authorization header containing CRLF or leading whitespace; will be monitored for 72 hours.

Security reviewed proposal to do on-the-fly header unfolding: currently rejected for private deployments due to risk of accepting modified tokens. Team will instead provide explicit diagnostics and vendor guidance.
Scheduled follow-up with AsterHealth for 2026-03-18 to verify stability and discuss preventative controls.
notes_for_followup: 1) Engineering to ship clearer ingress error message (PR #612) and ensure runbook contains vendor-specific guidance for F5/HAProxy/Nginx rules.
2) SRE to monitor alert for folded Authorization headers and escalate if frequency rises above 0.5%.
3) Customer success to confirm AsterHealth has scheduled proxy firmware update to latest vendor recommended build.
